REPLACE-REF COURT ADDENDUM — independent read-only reproduction, not a review of held cand-4E9. A pending candidate committed directly on main is detected by the current `rev-list --first-parent --parents` plus `NF==2` predicate. Replacing that tip with a same-tree two-parent commit makes Git render the original tip OID with two parents, so the predicate emits nothing. `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` restores the real one-parent object and the bypass is detected.

The successor court must also cover a custom replacement namespace. I placed the same replacement at `refs/evil/<tip>` and set `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE=refs/evil`; the bypass remained hidden. Therefore enumerating or refusing only `refs/replace/*` is not a complete defense. Exporting `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` before the first Git or Mote invocation defeated both default and custom-base attacks in the reproduction. Required court shape: default namespace attack, custom-base attack, same-mechanism no-replacement positive control, and a mutant removing the export. Exact scratch proof and OIDs are in chief FYI msg-01M1E5HJNMKQW7N3VC33F32GJS. No candidate verdict, source edit, policy amendment, authorization, or landing action is claimed.
